text: Robert Filipkowski4, Kevin Xu4, Steve Ferguson5, Resolute Bay Hunters and Trappers Association Resolute Bay 2016 – Qarmartalik School Workshop Activities Background We thank Peter Amarualik Sr., Nancy Amarualik, and Zipporah Aronsen for sharing their knowledge of ringed seals, David Idlout for providing the seal and Susan Salluviniq for translating. We also wish to thank all of the teachers and students at the Qarmartalik School for their participation and feedback.

1Environment and Climate Change Canada, 2Acadia University, 3 Nunavut Arctic College, 4Qarmartalik school Resolute Bay, 5Fisheries and Oceans Canada Scientists: Food webs and Contaminants in the North The ringed seal is a species of high cultural, economic and Scientists conducting research on ringed seal ecology and contaminants in the Canadian Arctic work towards better understanding the ecology and health of this species, often in collaboration with northern community members.
The Nunavut Environmental Contaminants Committee has recently suggested a need for increasing community engagement in contaminants research.

Goal: Conduct collaborative workshops to expand collaboration and communication between northern residents and scientific researchers working on contaminants in the Canadian Arctic Allow scientists studying contaminants in ringed seals to share information about their work with northern residents (with a focus on youth in particular).

Provide an opportunity for Inuit elders to share their knowledge with students and researchers in seal ecology and traditional methods for butchering seals, preparing seal skin and identifying abnormalities in harvested game.
Increase the engagement and interest of northern students in contaminants research and traditional seal harvesting.
Increase the capacity of northern residents (and Inuit youth, in particular) to engage in scientific research on northern contaminants.
